key_insight: Researchers are testing an AI tool that turns radiology results into plain-language summaries so oncology patients may better understand their scan findings.
clinical_relevance: If effective, the tool could improve patient communication in cancer care without adding substantial burden for oncology teams.
method: Embedded mixed-methods QI study with a randomized three-wave staircase rollout across oncology disease groups
About 60 providers from 11 disease focus groups plus two patient survey cohorts (350 pre-implementation, 350 post-implementation)
Provider surveys at 1 month pre-, 1 month post-, and 3 months post-implementation, plus patient and oncologist interviews
evidence_signal: This is a protocol paper, so the abstract reports planned surveys, interviews, and rollout evaluation rather than outcome results.
watch_item: AI-generated summaries will need careful oversight to avoid inaccuracies, over-simplification, or workflow friction in real-world oncology messaging.
paper_title: Implementing AI-assisted, patient-friendly imaging report summaries to enhance oncology care delivery: protocol for a randomized mixed-methods quality improvement study
